summary.text: A woman presented with chronic headache and swelling in the right parietal region that grew from 2 cm initially to up to 4 cm after 2 months. She had a history of head trauma from a motor vehicle accident nearly 4.5 years earlier. The case narrative gives her age as 32 and Table 1 as 33.

Skull radiographs showed a wide radiolucent area with sclerotic margins at the right parietal region, and MRI showed a round CSF-filled cystic mass, T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense. Postoperative coronal CT showed an internal table defect from an enlarged diploic space and a thinned external table.

Surgery used a modified curvilinear incision and craniotomy with drainage of the cystic contents; neuronavigation was deemed unnecessary. Total resection was performed and the bony defect was repaired with porous polyethylene. Histopathology showed an arachnoid/leptomeningeal cyst, and there were no complications.

summary.text: A 26-year old woman presented with headache and a smooth swelling palpable at the midline of her head. Examination found an oval, painful, soft mass 3 cm in diameter fixed to the skull at the vertex, with a normal neurological examination. CT showed a defect of the tabula interna with enlarged diploic space and complete destruction of the tabula externa.

MRI showed a round, lobulated cystic lesion in the right parasagittal region invading both tables and slightly compressing the superior sagittal sinus; T1 signal is described inconsistently in the source. The lesion was surgically removed using neuronavigational planning, a midline parasagittal incision and a high-speed drill, with cranioplasty using acrylic synthetic cement.

Lipid vacuoles were seen at the center on histopathological staining, and histopathological examination showed an intradiploic lipoma. Postoperatively all symptoms resolved and no adverse events were observed.

summary.text: An 18-year old boy presented with persistent headache following head trauma that occurred 3 months ago; another hospital reported that a cystic lesion had developed. MRI showed an intradiploic cystic mass in the parietal region, with signal descriptions that differ between the narrative and the Figure 9 caption.

He underwent surgery with excision of the intradiploic mass and reconstruction of the excision site with a titanium burr hole cap. Histopathological examination showed an eosinophilic granuloma, and chemotherapy was initiated after surgery.

A control CT revealed no abnormality requiring surgery, and the postoperative course was uneventful without new neurological deficits. The side of the lesion is stated inconsistently as right parietal or left parietal.

article_limitations: Table 2 (literature review) and the PRISMA diagram describe published cases and a database search, not patients of this series.

Patient 9: narrative sequence labels for Fig. 9B and 9D are swapped against the caption and Table 1; the narrative readings are review-only.
